messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] gets unexpected massage after loading package qtl and unexpected marker names(markers not in my actual file)  in summary scanone
parts:
1. If you type 'ls', R will print all of the code that defines the ls function. If you type 'ls()', R will execute that function. I think you left off the parentheses.

2. The default genotype codes for read.cross are "A", "H", "B"; if you've used different codes, you need to specify them via the 'genotypes' argument:

mycross <- read.cross("csv", file="myfile.csv", genotypes=c("AA", "AB", "BB"))

3. I'm guessing that you're referring to names like "c1.loc45", as in this example:

data(hyper)
hyper <-calc.genoprob(hyper, step=1)
out <- scanone(hyper)
summary(out, threshold=3)
## chr pos lod
## c1.loc45 1 48.3 3.53
## D4Mit164 4 29.5 8.09

We assess association between genotype and phenotype at the markers and at a set of "pseudomarkers", whose positions are determined by the 'step' argument in calc.genoprob(). Names like c1.loc45 are these pseudomarkers.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] gets unexpected massage after loading package qtl and unexpected marker names(markers not in my actual file) in summary scanone
parts:
Rather than do the calculations solely at the markers, we also consider positions between markers. This is in an attempt to get more precision information about the locations of QTL.

The summary output indicates the maximum LOD score on each chromosome and the position at which it was attained, which can be one of those pseudomarkers.

If you use step=0 in calc.genoprob, the calculations will be performed solely at the markers.

karl
